Here is the comprehensive technical prompt to build the described system from scratch:
Project Specification: High-Performance Distributed Audio Restoration System
Objective:
Construct a complete, production-ready web application for automated video and audio restoration. The system must utilize a distributed architecture where the frontend resides in a containerized environment (Replit-compatible) and the heavy computational backend operates on a high-performance cloud GPU cluster (Modal). The core signal processing must be implemented using the Faust functional DSP language, compiling to optimized C++ binaries for execution on the backend nodes.
Architecture Overview:
 * Frontend: A React-based Single Page Application (SPA) serving as the user interface for file uploads and status monitoring.
 * Backend: A Python-based serverless deployment using the Modal framework, orchestrating FFmpeg for media handling and executing compiled Faust binaries for signal processing.
 * DSP Engine: A Faust (.dsp) program implementing spectral noise gating, transient preservation, and dynamic range compression.
Detailed Implementation Instructions:
Step 1: Define the Environment and Dependencies (replit.nix)
Create a Nix configuration file to establish the build environment.
 * Include the following packages: pkgs.faust (for DSP compilation), pkgs.python311, pkgs.ffmpeg_6 (for media processing), pkgs.libsndfile, and pkgs.gcc.
 * Configure the LD_LIBRARY_PATH to ensure libsndfile and C++ standard libraries are accessible to the runtime.
Step 2: Implement the Digital Signal Processing Logic (cleaner.dsp)
Write a complete Faust program to process mono audio streams. The DSP chain must include the following stages in order:
 * Transient Protection: Implement a slew rate limiter (smoothing function) to reduce digital clicks and quantization noise without destroying transient attacks.
 * Spectral Filtering: Apply a high-pass filter at 80Hz to remove DC offset and rumble, and a low-pass filter at 15kHz to remove high-frequency hiss.
 * Noise Gate: Implement a spectral-style mono gate with a threshold of -20dB and fast attack/release times to silence background noise during pauses.
 * Compression: Implement a mono compressor with a 4:1 ratio to normalize vocal dynamics.
 * Makeup Gain: Apply linear gain correction to the output.
 * Ensure the code imports standard libraries (stdfaust.lib) and exposes necessary controls as compile-time variables or UI elements (though they will be hardcoded/automated in the backend).
Step 3: Construct the Distributed Backend (main.py)
Develop a Python script using the modal library to define the serverless infrastructure.
 * Infrastructure Definition:
   * Define a modal.Volume named "media-storage" for persisting video files across function calls.
   * Define a modal.Image based on Debian Slim. Install system dependencies: ffmpeg, libsndfile1, g++, make, and faust. Install Python dependencies: fastapi, python-multipart, uvicorn.
   * Define a modal.App named "crystal-clear-audio".
 * Processing Function:
   * Create a function decorated with @app.function.
   * Hardware: Configure this function to request high-performance GPU resources (specifically gpu="B200:1" or equivalent high-tier compute if available) to utilize associated high-bandwidth CPU and memory resources.
   * Logic:
     * Receive raw file bytes.
     * Write input video to the persistent volume.
     * Dynamically write the content of cleaner.dsp (from Step 2) to a file on the volume.
     * Use subprocess to extract audio from the video using FFmpeg (pcm_s16le format).
     * Use subprocess to compile the Faust code to a standalone sndfile binary using faust2sndfile.
     * Execute the compiled binary on the extracted audio to generate the processed wav file.
     * Use subprocess and FFmpeg to merge the original video stream with the processed audio stream, ensuring exact synchronization.
     * Return the binary content of the final MP4 file.
 * API Layer:
   * Create a FastAPI app instance.
   * Define a POST endpoint /clean that accepts an UploadFile.
   * Invoke the remote processing function (.remote()) and return the result as a Response with media_type="video/mp4".
   * Expose this via a modal_asgi_app decorator.
Step 4: Develop the Frontend Interface (App.jsx)
Create a React component file acting as the main entry point.
 * UI Design: Implement a clean, minimalist interface (white/gray color scheme). Avoid "sci-fi" or "cyberpunk" aesthetics. Use standard HTML/CSS or Tailwind classes.
 * Functionality:
   * State variables for file selection, loading status, and the result URL.
   * A file input area that accepts video files.
   * An "Upload/Start" button that is disabled during processing.
   * Network Request: An asynchronous function that sends the selected file to the Modal API endpoint (use a placeholder variable API_URL for the endpoint address).
   * Response Handling: Upon receiving the blob response, create an object URL and display a <video> player with controls and a download link.
Output Requirements:
Provide the full, unabridged code for every file: replit.nix, cleaner.dsp, main.py, and App.jsx. Do not omit imports, error handling, or implementation details. The code must be ready for immediate deployment and execution.
